candidate_relations.reason: No histology of adenoma or sarcoma is provided; sarcomatous transformation is a different entity from sellar cavernous hemangioma.
A germ-cell tumor is a distinct sellar/suprasellar neoplasm, not cavernous hemangioma.
Bitemporal field loss reflects chiasmal compression by the mass, not the histologic diagnosis.
Germinoma is a different germ-cell neoplasm from cavernous hemangioma.
Rathke cleft cyst is a related cystic sellar lesion with incompatible pathology versus cavernous hemangioma.
Pituitary adenoma is the referring impression for this sellar mass but is histologically incompatible with cavernous hemangioma.
Macroadenoma names the same incompatible pituitary epithelial tumor at large size.
Nonfunctioning adenoma matches the preoperative label, not the reference cavernous hemangioma.
There is no acute hemorrhagic pituitary crisis; the course is chronic over two years.
Pituitary carcinoma is a malignant epithelial neoplasm, not cavernous hemangioma.
Meningioma is a related extra-axial parasellar mass with different histology from cavernous hemangioma.
Adds chiasmal compression to adenoma, still an incompatible tumor type versus cavernous hemangioma.
Craniopharyngioma is a related sellar/suprasellar tumor, not cavernous hemangioma.
Hypophysitis is an inflammatory pituitary disorder, not a cavernous vascular neoplasm.
Same inflammatory entity, distinct from cavernous hemangioma.
Central hypothyroidism is endocrine mass effect, not the sellar vascular tumor.
